content: The recommended dosing for Airelle, Black Whortles, and Burren Myrtle Bilberry in combination is as follows: oral administration of 20-60 grams per day or 160 mg taken orally twice daily. The preparation contains 25% anthocyanosides. Alternatively, one cup can be taken orally, or 1 gram of dried leaf can be steeped in 150 ml of water. A 10% decoction can be applied topically as needed. Dried berries can also be boiled in water to prepare a decoction. This combination is indicated for the treatment of angina, atherosclerosis, circulatory problems, degenerative retinal conditions, diarrhea, mouth or throat inflammation (when used topically), retinopathy, and varicose veins. Clinical studies have demonstrated the efficacy of bilberry in managing diarrhea and retinopathy. Adverse effects include cachexia, anemia, and icterus. In animal studies, high doses have been associated with excitation. No adverse effects have been reported in humans. Regarding pregnancy, this combination is classified as Pregnancy Category A, meaning it is generally considered acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Information on lactation is not available.
